history.dynasty: Zamorins (Samoothiri) of Calicut; built in present form in the 14th century
history.period: Ancient lingam attributed to Parasurama (legend); present structure 14th century, renovated 1964
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 504 (Tali Mahakshetram) and seq 508 (Thali Maha Temple) - this is the same real temple, the Tali Shiva Temple at Palayam in the heart of Kozhikode city. Family temple of the Zamorins of Calicut; tradition holds Swamy Thirumulapad raised it within his palace complex and that the founding of Kozhikode is tied to the temple's rise, with the surrounding area called Kovilkota. The presiding deity is Shiva in Umamaheswara posture; the lingam is locally called a jyotirlingam, a self-manifested sacred lingam (note: NOT one of the 12 canonical Dwadasa Jyotirlingas). Damaged during the 18th-century Mysorean incursions (Tipu Sultan) and renovated in 1964. The temple hosts the annual Revathi Pattathanam scholarly gathering and is now under the Malabar Devaswom Board with the Zamorin as managing trustee.

name: Tali Maha Shiva Kshetram
town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is a major coastal city in northern Kerala and the historic seat of the Zamorin dynasty. A famed medieval trading port of the Malabar coast, it is known for its spices, the Mishkal Mosque, and rich Kathakali and football culture. It is well connected by rail, road, and the nearby Calicut International Airport.

travel.road: At Palayam, surrounded by Palayam market, in the heart of Kozhikode city; city buses and autos available
